steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You're...
Don't just stand there, come inside.
Let me show you around my room.
What do you think?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: You decorated it yourself?
Leonie helped.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: It's so spacious, and bright. Vivian... Your room is lovely.

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: Danke!

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: This room gets more sunlight than any other in the entire spire. As shy and lazy as Sturmland's sun is, it never feels too dark in here, even on the cloudiest days.

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: And then there's the veranda! It runs along the entire wall of the room. Look at that view... how far you can see... Look there.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: At what?

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: The green roof over there.

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: It's the Glenlossie Botanical Garden. Mutti took me there a few times. It has so many plants we don't see in Sturmland, or even greater Leithanien. But I love its roof the most.

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: Some Bolívarian claw-vines worked their way up there. It's probably too tall to easily get up onto the roof to trim them, so the staff just let them grow, and now they've covered the entire thing!

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: In springtime, clusters of pink flowers bloom from the vines, and the roof looks like a pink cloud. And now, in summertime, it's a deep green...

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: The leaves of those vines never drop. By autumn, the roof will turn gold, and in winter, only a perfect sheet of white will remain.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Ja, I can picture it now. Beautiful.

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: No matter how busy Vati was with his government work, he would always take time out of his day to come visit. Mutti would paint the scenery while he quietly told me their stories.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Vivian...

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: Yes?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Can you share those stories with me? Of Mutti and Vati?

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: That day in Marigold Alley, when he waited for her?

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: (Nod)

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: Vati said he was determined to say goodbye to her. But once he saw her, he couldn't bring himself to turn and go...

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: 'Vivian, if two hands are destined to join, why let the lands come between them?!' Ugh, so cheesy! Anyway, Vati brought Mutti back to Sturmland.

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: He stood... right there, beneath the spire, telling the worthies and bigwigs that if they didn't show Mutti the proper respect, he'd never return to Hochberg Spire again!

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: Nor would he succeed the Kurfürst.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: And did the nobles accede?

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: They did.

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: All because Vati stood below the spire for three whole days... Many men came to either change his mind or just shout at him, but none succeeded. They had no choice but to give in.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Werner von Hochberg protected his love, like a hero from a storybook.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: They were married with the blessings of everyone around them.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Viviana von Hochberg, your birth, too, won the blessings of all.

steps.name: Viviana
steps.text: Wunderbar.

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: Oh? What was that?

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: Is that Leonie? The door's open.
A maid walks in. Viviana looks to hide, but the maid goes straight for the little girl, as if she doesn't see Viviana at all.

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: Leonie, are you here for the carpet?

steps.name: Leonie
steps.text: *sigh*, Fräulein Droste, please step aside.

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: It's a masterpiece by a Minoan craftsman. Very comfortable under my feet, and the image of the lake and white walls on it is so vivid, I can almost feel the wind blowing when I look at it.

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: Mutti loved this carpet. She worked long and hard, scribing so many poems for others, just to be able to buy it.

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: When she left Zwillingstürme, she didn't bring much luggage with her, but she did bring this carpet.

steps.name: Leonie
steps.text: So... it would sell for a bit of money.

steps.name: Leonie
steps.text: You have to understand the Dame. This spire is otherwise empty; your room is the last decent thing in the place. If she could help it, the Dame wouldn't touch a thing in here.

steps.name: Leonie
steps.text: But since Kurfürst Werner's death, she has been troubled by all sorts of people. She's sold everything that could be sold...

steps.name: Leonie
steps.text: You're due to go study in Columbia, which takes no small amount of coin. She hopes you won't have to live in poverty abroad.

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: Oh, but, I could always not go.

steps.name: Leonie
steps.text: That won't do, Fräulein. You ought to leave Sturmland, to leave Leithanien.

steps.name: Leonie
steps.text: The Dame said as much to the Kurfürst two years ago, but it was only recently he gave the nod. You ought to set out soon, lest he change his mind.

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: What about Mutti? Can't she come with me?

steps.name: Leonie
steps.text: The Dame is at the Kurfürst's beck and call. She must remain in the spire.

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: I... I should speak to Onkel Schild.

steps.name: Leonie
steps.text: Fräulein, he may be your paternal uncle, but he is now Kurfürst of Sturmland.

steps.name: Leonie
steps.text: Just two years after the late Kurfürst Werner took the seat, he was assassinated while touring the domain. His marriage to the Dame offended a lot of people, and some have speculated it was Schild himself...

steps.name: Leonie
steps.text: Ugh, what am I thinking, why would I even tell you this?

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: Leonie... I have a question, and I'm not sure who to ask.

steps.name: Leonie
steps.text: Go ahead.

steps.name: Vivian
steps.text: If... if Mutti and Vati had lived an ordinary life, a commoner's life, would we have been happy?

steps.name: Leonie
steps.text: Fräulein... You've always been the sort of girl who... sees things as they are. You know what's going on.

steps.name: Leonie
steps.text: Pack your things. Put your beloved books and art collections into that rattan box there. I'll take care of the carpet and come back to put the rest in order.
The Elafia girl looks out at the city below the veranda. The wind is her only company now.
They say the roof of the Glenlossie Botanical Garden is beautiful. But what's there to appreciate when the night shrouds all?

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Frau Giallo?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It seems I really can't hear the voices anymore.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: No obvious wounds on you. Could your hearing be impaired?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: No. It's just much quieter than I'm used to...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Even as you're standing right in front of me, I still feel... so distant from you.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Oh? Is this a little better?

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Maybe I should speak louder?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: No, that's not it.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Let me take you somewhere nearby to rest. The ones chasing you should be far away by now.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Come, I'll help carry the cello.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Why are you gripping it so tightly? Your fingers are turning white!

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: It must be very important to you.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It is my eyes, my ears, my voice, and my heart.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I'm ashamed to admit it, but there was a time when I was even afraid of it.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Oh?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It took me some time to learn how to get along with it.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Soror? Why are you sitting in a dark corner with the lights out? Amita Luciana doesn't know you've come back.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Why did you skip cello practice after rowing in the park?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Oh, I'm sorry, I seem to have kicked your cello. The instrument is expensive. If I've damaged it... I have the money to compensate you.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Fede, take it away for me, will you?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Hide it anywhere you like. The study, the attic, in storage... You can even throw it away...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Are you crying?

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You played another piece you hadn't mastered yet.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I don't know... As soon as I draw my bow across its strings, I hear voices. So many voices.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: They're real voices, trapped in the bodies of men and women. They want to come out, and I should help them.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: But they're too loud, too chaotic.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: So many crying voices, laughing voices, whispering voices, voices furiously complaining... They all surge together...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: They're so loud, Fede! I can hardly breathe...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Are you unwell? Should I get Amita Luciana?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: I just... I just need some quiet...
The room is quiet, except for the isolated sobbing in the corner.
Two black halos look at each other, their cold, faint light being the only words they share.

a.text: Just be quiet for a while, just so my head doesn't hurt so much, just for a bit.
I will get used to the voices.
I just haven't mastered the skill yet...
It didn't take me long to learn to row a boat today. All I had to do was row it through the thick fog to the island in the center of the lake.
A song comes from the far shore.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Are you singing?

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: It's a folk song popular with buskers on this street. Heh, it's got a nice sound to it, but I'm a little tone-deaf, so...

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: When Jan would come home after being bullied, I'd comfort him with this song.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Thank you.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: You mentioned 'this street' just now?

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Oh, ja, Karl Schmidt Street. The people of Zwillingstürme also call it Marigold Alley.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Seniora Schüler, you haven't answered my question.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: According to the records of the Zwillingstürme Gendarmerie, Freiherr Fynn engaged in combat with a suspect to stop a kidnapping on Karl Schmidt Street in the autumn of 1085.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: The Baron was injured and unconscious for a period. When he awoke, both the suspect and the abducted Caprinae woman, twenty-seven-year-old Yulia Schüler, were missing.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Loris Bordin took over the case and conducted a series of investigations, finding no promising leads.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: He found the Baron's testimony suspicious, with the only certainty being that the Baron was the last person to see you.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: He strongly believed that a secret laid hidden within. Something like the Witch King's later experiments on Infected civilians, and that you had become the target of the Baron.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: But under pressure from above, the Gendarmerie halted any subsequent investigation and closed the case as an 'accidental disappearance.'

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: Loris Bordin took the case file back to his residence, and over the course of fifteen years, it has grown increasingly thick.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: He never gave up on investigating the truth, and never gave up on looking for you. Despite several clues indicating that Yulia Schüler was already deceased.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Hm...

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: You have just informed me that this here is Karl Schmidt Street.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: In other words, you came to the Genesis Horn posthumously, and currently exist as a form of 'consciousness.'

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: In your cognition, you have never left the scene of the incident.

steps.name: Federico
steps.text: So please tell me, what exactly happened in the course of that incident?

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: This is indeed Marigold Alley. We're standing in front of the piano studio at the intersection.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Oh, Herr Executor, we've wasted so much time. I really have to place these Arts devices in their proper places, quickly!

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Those masked men will be coming soon.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Do you mean to say that the Witch King's remains appear at various locations in Kargereich, according to some knowable set of rules?

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Ah, are they the Witch King's remains?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: No, they're not the ones in reality, sowing chaos in the name of the Witch King. What you see are but manifestations of the Witch King's craft, the 'Echoes of Herkunftshorn' in a truer sense.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: ...Klängenfolgen, to follow the sounds. That's the way to see the Witch King.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Why would the Witch King be in Zwillingstürme?

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Although I suppose it makes sense. I'm already dead, and the Witch King is too. So we're in the same place, that's logical enough.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: It would also explain all these strange happenings...

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Perhaps, having lost the sound of music, I can no longer perceive what you see in your eyes. Why do you call this place 'Zwillingstürme'?

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: ...Are you blind too?

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Frau Giallo, do you see the Musikinstrumententürme?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: The what?
Arturia looks in the direction the Caprinae woman is pointing, and sees nothing but vague light and shadow.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Reichsmusikhochschule has towers, die Musikinstrumententürme. But only eleven.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Reichsmusikhochschule is the most famous landmark in Bachshof. Each spire of the royal academy is inspired by a musical instrument, and was named for it upon completion.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: There are eleven instruments, and when Herr Bach presided over his 'Glorreiches Kapitalprojekt,' a grand urban plan, he added eleven more.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Twenty-two instrument spires corresponding to the twenty-two districts of Zwillingstürme, like a perfect symphony orchestra.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Hah, you know your stuff.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Ja, but there are only eleven Musikinstrumententürme here. This is not the Reichsmusikhochschule of Zwillingstürme, but that of the Witch King's time.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: And behind us... is a tilted spire, circular, the color of jade.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: 'Der Schiefer Turm der Ewigkeit.' The Leaning Tower of Eternity?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: It was originally the spire of some Kurfürst or other. It began to lean due to changes in the strata, and with the support of the magnificent Arts of the spire casters, it maintained its baffling tilt without collapsing.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: This miracle of Leithanian architecture was destroyed in a Catastrophe, four centuries ago...

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Not only that. I see Der Wiener Uhrturm, Das auf den Kopf gestellte Strafgebäude, Die Tür des Wissens, Der Schönbrunnturm...

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Countless spires of different eras, forms, and functions. I've only read about them in books, or heard of them in stories from my elders...

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: But here, they all stand.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: This isn't Zwillingstürme, but it's not Vedunien either. I think the most proper name for it would be... 'Leithanien.'

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: The only part that feels familiar is the Marigold Alley beneath my feet. At the intersection sits a piano studio, at the end of the street is an art gallery, and right in the middle is my cafe.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: I'm glad they're still here. I've rediscovered them.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Here, I can still live just the way I used to. So, unfamiliar as this place is, I would still rather call it Zwillingstürme.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Maybe you haven't rediscovered your old life.

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: Rather, it's because of your life that you came to be here.

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Oh!

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: There are only nine Musikinstrumententürme left... When did the Klavierturm and the Waldhornturm vanish?

steps.name: Arturia
steps.text: (Herr Fremont was right, the Genesis Horn is accelerating its collapse...)

steps.name: Yulia
steps.text: Frau Giallo, do you... see it now?
